findings.title: Per-visitor rate limits include the caller-controlled User-Agent, so they are bypassable and the global order cap can be drained
findings.route: Every public write: /korpa checkout (orders:submit, carts cartCreate), /upit (inquiries:submit, inquiries:generateUploadUrl), back-in-stock subscribe, consent:record, search:log, /za-majstore (mechanics:register), quick order
findings.context: Dev deployment, anonymous ConvexHttpClient from one machine and IP with a custom fetch that sets the User-Agent header. Harmless mutation used (issuing an upload URL writes no business record).
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/backend-ratelimit-ua.mjs`.
21 calls to inquiries:generateUploadUrl with one fixed User-Agent: 20 succeed and the 21st returns RATE_LIMITED (limit uploadUrl, 20/h per client).
21 more calls from the same IP, each with a different User-Agent: all 21 succeed, 0 limited.
findings.expected: Per-visitor limits hold for a given IP whatever headers the caller sends. No single public limit can be drained by one client to lock out every other customer.
findings.actual: The key is SHA-256(salt|ip|UA) (convex/lib/functions.ts:26-36, D4), and changing the UA gives a fresh bucket. The audit kit itself relies on this. Honeypot and the 3 s startedAt are client-supplied, so a script can submit unlimited inquiries and uploads (8 MB each) and create guest carts. It can also place orders until orderSubmitGlobal (fixed window, 300/h, convex/lib/rateLimits.ts:13) trips, after which every genuine customer gets „Previše pokušaja“ until the hour resets.
findings.suggested_fix: In getClientInfo (convex/lib/functions.ts), key per-client limits on the IP alone: salted hash, with the /64 prefix for IPv6. Keep the UA out of the key, or use ip+UA only as a second, finer bucket. Size the per-IP buckets for carrier NAT. Turn orderSubmitGlobal into a high alarm threshold that notifies the owner instead of a hard stop that blocks customers, or require sign-in/extra checks only above it. Add a convex-test proving two UAs from one IP share a bucket.
findings.standard: BRIEF §9 Security („rate limits on public writes“), SECURITY §L2, D4 (intent: real client IP limits)

verification.notes:
Reproduced independently with my own script, which uses a new UA prefix and a new ConvexHttpClient per call, against the harmless inquiries:generateUploadUrl (uploadUrl, 20/h per client key). (A) 21 calls with one fixed UA: 20 ok, the 21st RATE_LIMITED. (B) 10 calls, each with a new UA: 10 ok, 0 limited. (C) Control: the fixed UA from A again, 2 calls: both RATE_LIMITED. So the IP did not change between A and B, and B passed because of the UA alone. (D) Fixed UA plus a trailing space: still limited (header whitespace is normalised), so the UA really has to be different.

Skeptic checks:
- The key design is documented: D4, ARCHITECTURE §E6 and SECURITY.md D3 all say clientKey = SHA-256(salt + ip + UA). No reason for including the UA is written down.
- The bypass is not listed as an accepted risk in SECURITY-AUDIT §2.4 (R01–R11).
- The team knows about it and uses it only for tests: the te…
evidence: docs/qa/audit/verify/backend/backend-02-skeptic.json (A: 20 ok + RATE_LIMITED; B: 10/10 ok; C control: 2/2 RATE_LIMITED; D: 3/3 RATE_LIMITED)
convex/orders.ts:60-61 — orderSubmitGlobal enforced before the per-client orderSubmit; rolled back when the submit fails
convex/inquiries.ts:136 — only inquirySubmit per ctx.client.key; no per-e-mail or global inquiry limit
convex/events.ts:411-423 — inquiry.created sends inquiry_received to inquiry.contact.email (caller-supplied)
tests/e2e/storefront.spec.ts:21 — 'A unique user agent per run gives fresh per-client rate-limit buckets in Convex'
docs/DECISIONS.md D4 / docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §E6 — key design documented without a rationale for the UA; not in SECURITY-AUDIT §2.4 accepted risks
corrected_steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/verify-backend-02-skeptic.mjs` (anonymous ConvexHttpClient, custom User-Agent header, mutation inquiries:generateUploadUrl, no records written).
Phase A: 21 calls with one fixed UA. The first 20 return ok and the 21st returns RATE_LIMITED.
Phase B: 10 calls from the same machine and IP, each with a new UA. All 10 return ok.
Phase C (control): 2 more calls with the fixed UA from phase A. Both return RATE_LIMITED, which proves the IP did not change and the bypass comes from the UA alone.

Code path for impact: inquiries:submit is limited only by inquirySubmit on the same client key, and each accepted inquiry queues an inquiry_received e-mail to the submitted contact.email. So rotating the UA allows unlimited inquiries and confirmation e-mails to arbitrary addresses. The global order cap can only be drained with about 300 successful orders per hour, because failed submits roll back their global token.

findings.title: Home FAQ restricts the statutory 14-day withdrawal right and contradicts the site's own legal page
findings.route: / (Česta pitanja → „Mogu li da vratim deo?“) vs /reklamacije-i-povrat
findings.context: All viewports, anonymous; home is the main ad landing
steps: Open / and scroll to „Česta pitanja“

findings.title: 3D start freezes the main thread for 0.3–0.9 s at the visitor's first touch, scroll or hover (the PMREM shader compiles synchronously, the first frame still links programs, the 3D chunk evaluates)
findings.context: Chromium 1.63 headless, ANGLE D3D11 (RTX 4060 Laptop). Desktop 1440×900 at DPR 1, CPU 1× and 4×. Mobile 390×844 at DPR 3 with touch, CPU 4× and 6×. Anonymous visitor, consent answered, first visit (fresh browser, so the GPU program cache is cold). Server: localhost:3200.
steps: Launch a fresh Chromium with --use-angle=d3d11 --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist and open http://localhost:3200/. Wait for load.
Optional: set the CPU throttle with CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate {rate: 4}.
Give intent: on desktop move the pointer over the hero stage; on mobile tap the stage or scroll more than 40 px.

Record a CPU profile and the long tasks until window.__sklop3d.getState().status === 'ready'. Scripted: `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-profile.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 1 --gpu`, run 3 times (each run launches a new browser); `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-frames.mjs --vp mobile --cpu 4 --gpu --runs 3`; and `... --cold` to make the first scroll the intent.
findings.expected: The 3D never blocks the page. The init runs in short tasks (WEB-QA §4 records tasks ≤ 175 ms), and compileAsync plus idle slices keep scrolling and taps responsive while the model comes up (BRIEF §4, contract F7.3).
findings.actual: PMREMGenerator.fromEquirectangular → _applyGGXFilter → getUniforms → getProgramParameter blocks while the PMREM blur shader compiles: 336, 344 and 457 ms at 1× CPU on three fresh browsers (busy stretches 378–519 ms), and 725–884 ms at 4×. The 3D chunk (282 KB gzip) takes 255–345 ms to evaluate at 4×. The first real frame after compileAsync still blocks 160–190 ms in getProgramParameter plus 52–92 ms of texSubImage2D, although KHR_parallel_shader_compile is available. Worst start long task: desktop 4× 556/291/434 ms (start TBT 604–1113 ms); mobile 4× 765/294/313 ms (TBT 527–1603 ms); mobile 6× 897/435/616 ms (TBT 1267–2293 ms). When the first scroll on a phone is the intent (4×), a single frame in the middle of the scroll takes 683, 333 and 300 ms (3/3 runs). A warm program cache cuts the PMREM cost to about 77 ms, but first-time visitors (ad traffic) always pay the full cost.
findings.suggested_fix: components/three/canvas/loadCar.ts loadEnvironment(): stop prefiltering at runtime. Bake the PMREM output (cubeUV layout) in the 3D pipeline, export it as a half-float/RGBE PNG or KTX2, load it with mapping = CubeUVReflectionMapping and drop PMREMGenerator and HDRLoader. If that is not possible, compile the PMREM blur material through KHR_parallel_shader_compile first (compileAsync on a throwaway mesh) before calling fromEquirectangular. In HeroCanvas.tsx, include every material the first frame uses (edge and depth materials, overlay layer) in the compileAsync pass, and initTexture every texture before compileAsync. On fine-pointer devices, import and evaluate the canvas chunk in idle time before intent. Then correct the numbers in docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §4.
findings.standard: BRIEF §4 (the 3D must never block the page); 3D-CONTRACT F7.3 (compileAsync, idle slices); DESIGN-SYSTEM §1 principle 5 (3D never blocks); docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §4 (init in tasks ≤ 175 ms); INP ≤ 200 ms

verification.notes: CPU profile on a fresh browser at 1×: PMREM fromEquirectangular → getProgramParameter is a busy stretch of 390 ms (350 ms self), and the first frame after compileAsync 242 ms (148 ms getProgramParameter). A warm program cache in the same browser cuts this to 15 ms and 76 ms. At 4×, cold: PMREM 558 ms, first frame and compileAsync 357 ms, canvas chunk evaluation 178 ms. Frames runs, worst start long task: mobile 4× 520/389/230 ms (sum over 50 ms 936/652/381), desktop 4× 472/199/228 ms (818/324/425). This contradicts WEB-QA §4's 'tasks ≤ 175 ms'. Lowered to P2: the freeze follows an explicit intent, happens once per cold visit and blocks no flow; BRIEF's 'never block the page' is about loading after first paint, which holds. The --cold first-scroll case was not re-run.

Analysis only: I ran no browser. I re-read the finder's and the perf verifier's JSON and profiles with an offline script, then checked the code. CONFIRMED: on a first visit (cold GPU program cache), Windows ANGLE D3D11 compiles the PMREM GGX shader synchronously. loadCar.ts:96-105 calls pmrem.fromEquirectangular(), which uses the three 0.186.1 GGX filter with a 256-sample loop. Nothing precompiles it; compileAsync in HeroCanvas.tsx:126 covers only the scene materials. At 1x CPU this is a single getProgramParameter wait of 336/344/457 ms (finder, 3 launches) and 350 ms (verifier). The first frame after compileAsync adds 138-191 ms. With a warm cache in the same browser, desktop 1x start TBT drops from 525 ms (run 0) to 8/0 ms (runs 1-2). The shader compile alone is enough to explain the 1x cost. The compile time does not depend on the network, so this is not a localhost artefact. NARROWER…

Use a NEW browser launch for every measured run: a new context in the same browser reuses the in-memory GPU program cache, and the problem disappears.
Open http://localhost:3200/ at 1440x900, DPR 1, CPU 1x, with consent answered. Wait for load.
Move the pointer over the hero stage (intent). Record a CPU profile until window.__sklop3d.getState().status === 'ready'.

A second task of about 200-250 ms follows (138-191 ms getProgramParameter in the first render after compileAsync). Start TBT is about 525 ms.
Control: repeat in the same browser (warm cache). Start TBT is 0-8 ms at 1x, and PMREM takes about 15 ms.

Do not count the canvas chunk evaluation (turbopack H, about 20 ms at 1x, 255-489 ms at 4x/6x) toward this finding. It is the budgeted lazy chunk. Phone numbers need a real phone GPU backend, not a desktop D3D11 run with CPU throttling.

Add a Playwright regression: 3 home ↔ /delovi cycles, forced GC, a WeakRef on the hero canvas must be empty and Performance.getMetrics Nodes must stay flat.

findings.title: High tier renders 4× MSAA at up to DPR 2: estimated GPU memory is 62 MB at DPR 1 and 114–194 MB on HiDPI screens, against a 60 MB budget
findings.context: Desktop 1440×900, high tier, DPR 1 and DPR 2 (HiDPI laptop), ANGLE D3D11, CPU 4×. GPU memory is estimated by instrumenting bufferData, texStorage2D, texImage2D and renderbufferStorage, plus the drawing buffer (RGBA8 + depth per sample × 4 samples + resolve).
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-frames.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 4 --gpu --runs 3 --dpr 2 --tag desktop-dpr2-cpu4-gpu` and read gl.perContext in the JSON.
Or in DevTools: document.querySelector('[data-testid=hero-track] canvas') → width/height, and getContext('webgl2').getContextAttributes().antialias.
findings.expected: 3D-CONTRACT F5: GPU memory ≤ 60 MB on desktop.
findings.actual: Resources are 20.7 MB (buffers 5.9 MB in 643 buffers, textures 14.8 MB in 13 textures) and would pass alone. The MSAA drawing buffer adds 41.3 MB at 1440×836 DPR 1, for 62.1 MB total. On a DPR 2 screen, after the adaptive step to 1.5 (2160×1254), it adds 93 MB for 113.7 MB total. Before that step, at 2880×1672, it is about 173 MB, or about 194 MB total. The cause is `antialias: tier === "high"` combined with `dpr={[1, 2]}`. Same numbers in 3/3 runs.
findings.suggested_fix: components/three/canvas/HeroCanvas.tsx: use MSAA only when the effective DPR is below 1.5 (antialias: tier === 'high' && window.devicePixelRatio < 1.5), or cap the high tier at DPR 1.5 when MSAA is on. At DPR 2 without MSAA the drawing buffer is about 38 MB, so the total is about 59 MB, and integrated GPUs (the typical high-tier laptop) get the fill-rate back. Also state in the contract whether the drawing buffer counts toward the budget.
findings.standard: 3D-CONTRACT F5 (GPU memory ≤ 60 MB)

verification.notes: GPU estimate at DPR 1 (1440×836) is 62.1 MB in 3 of 3 frames runs plus the leak run. At DPR 2, after the adaptive step to 1.5 (canvas 2160×1254), it is 113.7 MB. At 2880×1672 before that step, the drawing buffer alone works out to about 173 MB (4× MSAA color + depth + resolve). Cause confirmed in code: HeroCanvas.tsx sets antialias: tier === "high" with dpr={[1, TIER_MAX_DPR[tier]]}, and high is 2. The contract does not say whether the drawing buffer counts toward the 60 MB budget.

findings.context: Chromium 1440×900, shared customer account, production build on :3100. Cookie values fingerprinted only (SHA-256 prefix).
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/audit/backend-session-refresh.mjs`: sign in, then 6 full page loads about 3 s apart.

findings.standard: BRIEF §9 Reliability/Performance (no needless backend work per request), SECURITY §D1 (1 h JWT, refresh only near expiry)

findings.title: Desktop explode scroll at 4× CPU misses the documented WEB-QA smoothness bar: 290 draws per frame, and the X-ray two-pass recomputes program keys every frame
findings.context: Desktop 1440×900, DPR 1, high tier, ANGLE D3D11 (RTX 4060), CPU 4×, 60 wheel steps through the whole hero track. Mobile 390 @ 3×, mid tier, CPU 4× and 6×.
steps: Run `node scripts/qa/hero-frames.mjs --base http://localhost:3200 --cpu 4 --gpu` 3 times. This is the WEB-QA script, uninstrumented.
Run `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-frames.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 4 --gpu --runs 3` to get draws and triangles per frame, and `--vp mobile --cpu 6` for the low-end phone profile.
Run `node scripts/qa/audit/perf-3d-profile.mjs --vp desktop --cpu 4 --gpu --phase scroll` for the CPU attribution.
findings.expected: docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §1: at 4× CPU, median 16.7 ms, p95 ≤ 33 ms and ≤ 6 % of frames over 33 ms (recorded as Pass). 3D-CONTRACT F5: 60 fps on desktop while scrubbing; draw calls ≤ 220 (desktop) and ≤ 150 (lite); lite ≤ 250 k triangles.
findings.actual: Uninstrumented desktop runs: p95 50.0 / 33.4 / 50.0 ms, frames over 33 ms 7.9 / 4.6 / 8.1 %, worst 83–100 ms, 10–21 long tasks. Instrumented runs: 8.8 / 8.4 / 16.4 %, p95 50–67 ms. So 5 of 6 runs miss the bar. At 1× the desktop is perfect (p95 16.7 ms, 0 %). Per frame: 290 draw calls and 416 k triangles on desktop (the GLB itself is 213 draws and 344 k), because the edges add hidden + depth + visible passes per shell mesh. Mobile: 172 draws and 257 k triangles per frame (lite budget 150 and 250 k). Mobile 4× passes (1.3–4.6 %), but mobile 6× has 21.8 / 32.6 / 25.1 % of frames over 33 ms (p95 67–100 ms). CPU profile at 4×: the main thread is busy 5.37 s out of 9.91 s, and three's render takes 73 % of that. getParameters (390 ms) + getProgramCacheKey (116 ms) of self time come from X-ray materials that use transparent + DoubleSide: three's automatic two-pass sets material.needsUpdate = true twice per object per frame.
findings.suggested_fix: components/three/canvas/materials.ts createXrayMaterial: replace side: DoubleSide and three's automatic two-pass with two explicit materials: BackSide at 0.5× alpha rendered first through renderOrder, then FrontSide. Alternatively use forceSinglePass plus a back-face clone. Either way needsUpdate is never set per frame. components/three/canvas/enhance.ts: stop adding 3 draws per shell mesh. Precompute the edge lines in the pipeline as one line primitive per part node, and drop the separate depth pre-pass by letting the front-face shell pass write depth for the visible-edge test. Re-measure with hero-frames.mjs and correct docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §1.
findings.standard: 3D-CONTRACT F5 (runtime 60 fps desktop while scrubbing; draw-call and lite triangle budgets); docs/3d/WEB-QA.md §1 scroll smoothness bar

verification.notes: The smoothness-bar miss did not reproduce. So 4 of 5 runs meet the ≤ 6 % bar, against the finder's 5 of 6 misses. Mobile 4×: 2.3–6.6 % instrumented, 0.7/5.5 % uninstrumented. The per-frame counts are confirmed: desktop 290 draws and 416,272 triangles, mobile 172 draws and 257,044 triangles, against the F5 figures of 220 and 150 draws and the lite 250 k triangles. Those budgets are defined for the GLB after merging, which is 213 draws, so how runtime passes count against them is open to interpretation. I did not re-measure mobile 6× or the getProgramCacheKey profile.
